name: Group theory from the solution of polynomial equations
summary: Permutations of roots, first a tool for solving equations, become an object studied for its own structure and are then axiomatised independently of permutations.
currentKeyWorks: J.-L. Lagrange, Reflexions sur la resolution algebrique des equations, Nouv. Mem. Acad. Berlin (1770-71)
N. H. Abel, J. reine angew. Math. 1 (1826)
E. Galois, Memoire sur les conditions de resolubilite des equations par radicaux (1831; publ. J. Math. Pures Appl. 11 (1846), in Liouville's edition of the Oeuvres, 381-444)
A. Cayley, On the theory of groups, as depending on the symbolic equation theta^n = 1, Phil. Mag. 7 (1854)
C. Jordan, Traite des substitutions et des equations algebriques (1870)
H. Weber, Math. Ann. 43 (1893)
Lagrange, Reflexions sur la resolution algebrique (1770)
Vandermonde (1771)

name: The probabilistic method in combinatorics
summary: Existence of a combinatorial object is proved by showing a random object has the property with positive probability.
currentKeyWorks: P. Erdos, Some remarks on the theory of graphs, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 53 (1947)
P. Erdos and A. Renyi, On random graphs I, Publ. Math. Debrecen 6 (1959)
N. Alon and J. Spencer, The Probabilistic Method (1992)
Erdos, Some remarks on the theory of graphs (Bull. AMS 1947)

name: Hodge theory proves log-concavity conjectures
summary: Heron-Rota-Welsh log-concavity of chromatic polynomials and Rota's conjecture are proved using Hodge-Riemann relations on Chow rings of matroid-like objects.
currentKeyWorks: J. Huh, Milnor numbers of projective hypersurfaces and the chromatic polynomial of a graph, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 25 (2012)
J. Huh and E. Katz, Log-concavity of characteristic polynomials and the Bergman fan of matroids, Math. Ann. 354 (2012)
K. Adiprasito, J. Huh and E. Katz, Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries, Ann. of Math. 188 (2018)
Adiprasito-Huh-Katz, Hodge theory for combinatorial geometries, Annals 2018 (arXiv:1511.02888)
Huh-Katz, Log-concavity of characteristic polynomials and the Bergman fan of matroids, Math.Ann. 2012

name: Non-Euclidean geometry: the independence of the parallel postulate
summary: After Saccheri and Lambert explored denials of the fifth postulate, Gauss privately, then Bolyai and Lobachevsky openly, developed a consistent geometry with many parallels.
currentKeyWorks: Bolyai, appendix to Farkas Bolyai's book (c. 1825)
Lobachevsky, Kazan Messenger (1829)
Lobachevsky, Geometrical investigations on the theory of parallels (1840)
Lobachevsky (Kazan Messenger, 1829)
Bolyai, Appendix (1831)

name: Erdos discrepancy
summary: Tao used Polymath5's reduction and Fourier/entropy methods for multiplicative functions to settle the Erdos discrepancy problem; SAT solvers had done the c=2 case earlier.
currentKeyWorks: Tao, The Erdos discrepancy problem, Discrete Analysis 2016 (arXiv:1509.05363)
Konev-Lisitsa, A SAT attack on the Erdos discrepancy conjecture, 2014

name: Lenstra-Lenstra-Lovasz lattice basis reduction
summary: Geometry-of-numbers ideas give a polynomial-time algorithm that factors polynomials and attacks integer programming and knapsack cryptosystems.
currentKeyWorks: A. K. Lenstra, H. W. Lenstra, L. Lovasz, Factoring polynomials with rational coefficients, Math. Ann. 261 (1982)

name: Differential equations from calculus
summary: Newton solved fluxional equations by series; Leibniz separated variables; Bernoullis solved named equations.
currentKeyWorks: Newton, Methodus Fluxionum (1671)
Jacob Bernoulli (1695)

name: Positive Grassmannian as a hub between combinatorics, probability and integrable systems
summary: Total positivity extended to the Grassmannian produced cell-counting polynomials that also give probabilities in exclusion processes and describe soliton solutions of the KP equation.
currentKeyWorks: Lusztig and Postnikov (c. 1998-2006, per article)
Corteel-Williams on exclusion processes

name: Steinitz abstract field theory
summary: Steinitz gave the first abstract definition of field and proved every field has an algebraic closure.
currentKeyWorks: Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Koerper, Crelle 1910

name: Category theory
summary: Natural isomorphisms noticed in homology computations are formalised as functors and natural transformations, and the resulting structure becomes a general language.
currentKeyWorks: S. Eilenberg and S. Mac Lane, General theory of natural equivalences, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 58 (1945)
S. Mac Lane, Categories for the Working Mathematician (1971)
Eilenberg-Mac Lane, General theory of natural equivalences (1945)
